evidence.estrutura: Zetkin organized through socialist parties, unions and mass movements rather than advocating personalist executive rule; her socialism nevertheless accepted strong collective institutions, so neither radical federalism nor unitary authoritarianism alone fits.
evidence.representacao: She campaigned for women’s suffrage and represented socialist and communist parties in parliamentary institutions, supporting mass political participation.
evidence.poder: Her opposition to wartime repression and work in socialist opposition politics weigh against unchecked coercive authority, though she accepted revolutionary political organization.
evidence.imigracao: Her socialist internationalism emphasized class solidarity across nations and weighs against ethnic-national exclusion; no detailed immigration statute program is documented.
evidence.diplomacia: Her break with pro-war social democrats and anti-war organizing strongly support an anti-militarist orientation.
evidence.intervencao: Internationalist socialism and opposition to imperial war support anti-imperial and relatively non-interventionist foreign politics.
evidence.economia: Her politics were explicitly socialist and tied women’s emancipation to transformation of capitalist property relations.
evidence.controle: Socialist economic coordination and labor organization support high public/collective control, short of evidence for Stalinist command administration.
evidence.comercio: Her internationalism was not liberal free-trade doctrine; nationalist protectionism was also not central. Keep trade moderately internationalist.
evidence.religiao: Her Marxist political framework was secular and did not ground public authority in religion.
evidence.moral: Women’s emancipation, suffrage and equality place her strongly on the progressive gender side.
evidence.tecnologia: Industrial modernity was treated through class politics rather than a distinct technology ideology; moderate modernist placement.
